lines.text: Today AI drafts your slides and posters in minutes, and you make them look like your brand.
Ask a chatbot for a 6-slide outline: a title for each slide, 3 short points, and speaker notes.
Check the facts and change the order until the story makes sense.
A good outline makes every slide tool easier.
In Canva, look for its AI design option and paste your outline to get a ready deck.
In PowerPoint or Google Slides, make one slide per title and paste the points, then use the design suggestions.
Some AI features are limited on free plans.
Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT and Canva can make an image from a description.
Say the subject, style, colours and shape, like square for Instagram.
AI images often get words wrong, so ask for no text and add the words yourself.
Use the same two or three colours, one or two fonts and your logo on every slide and post.
Label AI-made images, for example “Image made with AI”.
Never make fake photos of real people, fake reviews, or pictures of products that look better than the real thing.
We start with the story, not the design, by asking for a six-slide outline.
The outline has a title and three short points for each slide, plus speaker notes.
Read it like a manager: is anything wrong for your shop, and is the order right?
In Canva, search for a presentation and use the AI design option with your outline.
Pick a design you like, then switch the colours and fonts to your brand.
If the AI option is not available to you, choose any template and paste the points in yourself.
You can also paste the outline into PowerPoint or Google Slides, one slide per title.
Use the design suggestions or a theme, and keep your speaker notes under each slide.
Now a social media post: we describe the subject, the colours, the style and the shape.
The picture looks lovely, but the words at the top are misspelt.
Image tools are often bad at spelling, so ask for no text in the image.
Then add your words, prices and logo in Canva, where you control every letter.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
